newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's September tax collection fall by 29 pct.
newsitem.headline: Russia's September tax collection fall by 29 pct.

text.p: Tax revenues in September fell 29 percent from August levels to 9.33 trillion roubles, Prime-Tass news agency quoted State Tax Service officials as saying on Tuesday.
In September the government collected only 45 percent of budgeted taxes while taxes for the first nine months of the year were running at 75 percent of budgeted levels, it said.
State Tax Service officials told Prime-Tass the low collection rate was due to a growing non-payment crisis, crippling the Russian economy.
Many companies and government agencies are simply not paying their bills to each other, creating a web of debt.

The authorities have said they will step up pressure on major companies to pay their taxes. Last week the chairman of Russia's biggest company, Gazprom, said the tax authorities had frozen assets of some of its subsidiaries to force it to pay tax arrears.
Tax undercollection is one of the most serious problems facing Russia.
The International Monetary Fund delayed payment of a tranche of its $10 billion loan in July because it was worried about the budget deficit.
Economy Minister Yevgeny Yasin told Prime-Tass that he expected a rise in revenues in October or November.
He said the Economy Ministry was working on a new Tax Code, which would help increase tax collectibility.
Taxes which are easier to collect and least burdensome for tax-payers, such as Value Added Tax, will become a priority, Yasin said.
